provenance.what: Answerability verdicts, one per case, each given from the case request and the `rendered` text beside it and nothing else. Not a production judge; for replay only.
provenance.rubric: yes: the text alone gives the reader everything the request asked for. partial: it gives some of it, or something the request asked for shows only on a richer surface. no: it does not give what the request asked for.
provenance.stale: The replay judge returns the recorded verdict, and lists the case under staleJudgments in baseline.json when the text rendering no longer matches `rendered`; re-judge those cases.

comparison.rendered:
SELF-MANAGED VS. SERVERLESS

SERVERLESS HANDS UPGRADES AND SCALING TO ELASTIC
Self-managed keeps every knob in your hands; Serverless trades that control for less to operate and a bill that follows usage.

CONCERN     SELF-MANAGED ELASTICSEARCH                     ELASTIC CLOUD SERVERLESS
----------  ---------------------------------------------  -----------------------------------------------
Upgrades    Your team plans, tests, and rolls them         Elastic applies them continuously
Scaling     You size nodes and add capacity ahead of load  Scales automatically with ingest and query load
Cost model  Pay for the infrastructure you provision       Pay for what you ingest, store, and query

MARCH 4 INCIDENT TIMELINE

AN EXPIRED CERTIFICATE TOOK 66 MINUTES TO CLEAR
From the first alert at 02:14 to all clear at 03:20 on March 4.

02:14 · ALERT. “Alert fired” Monitoring raised the first alert.
02:16 · PAGE. “On-call paged” The on-call engineer was paged two minutes later.
02:51 · DIAGNOSIS. “Root cause found” An expired TLS certificate.
03:05 · FIX. “Fix deployed” The certificate fix went out.
● 03:20 · RESOLVED. “All clear” Service confirmed healthy.

process.rendered:
OUR RELEASE PROCESS

EVERY CHANGE REACHES 5% OF USERS BEFORE IT REACHES EVERYONE
A pull request passes CI and two reviews, ships in the nightly build, and rolls out in stages.

Pull request → CI → Two approvals → Merge to main → Nightly build → 5% rollout → All users
1. CI — Tests and checks run on the pull request.
2. Two approvals — Two reviewers approve before it can merge.
3. Merge to main — The change lands on main.
4. Nightly build — That night’s build picks it up.
5. 5% rollout — A staged rollout to 5% of users first.
